Here’s a quick rundown of J.K. Rowling’s most well‑known titles: | Series / Work | Publication Year(s) | Notes | |---------------|---------------------|-------| | **Harry Potter** (main series) | 1997–2007 | Seven core novels plus companion guidebooks (“Fantastic Beasts & Where to Find Them,” “Quidditch Through the Ages”). These have sold over 500 million copies worldwide and spawned an entire film franchise. | | *Harry Potter* spin‑offs | – | • **“Harry Potter and the Cursed Child”** (play script, 2016)
• **“Harry Potter: A History of Magic”** (illustrated book, 2018) | | **Cormoran Strike** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2011–present | Detective fiction featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike. First novel, *"The Cuckoo's Calling,"* was shortlisted for the Edgar Award. | | **Other Novels** | – | • **“The Casual Vacancy”** (2012) – Rowling’s first adult novel outside the Harry Potter universe.
• **“The Ickabog”** (2020) – a children’s fable released as a free online story before print publication. | ### Why they’re popular - **Cultural impact:** The Harry Potter saga reshaped modern fantasy literature and created a massive global fanbase. - **Critical acclaim:** Both the main series and the Cormoran Strike mysteries received numerous literary awards and nominations. - **Cross-media presence:** From films and theme park attractions to merchandise and stage productions, Rowling’s work has permeated multiple entertainment platforms. If you’d like more details on any particular title or authorial pseudonym, let me know!
